Definition: properly, a failure of, i.e. (used only as a negative particle, usually with a prepositional prefix) not, except, without, unless, besides, because not, until, etc.
BiblicalUsage: Not, except, without, unless — this is the small word that draws the lines of the whole Bible, and it appears over a hundred times. In Genesis 3:11 God asks, who told thee that thou wast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat? In Exodus 20:20 Moses says fear not, for God is come to prove you. In Amos 3:3 the prophet asks, can two walk together, except they be agreed? And in Deuteronomy 12:23 the law says, only be sure that thou eat not the blood.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this little word carries the whole weight of obedience: not, except, unless — the lines God draws are the lines that keep his people alive.
